claims.sourceText: Stringfield, Status Report III, 'Chronology of cases reported in the UFO Crash/Retrieval Syndrome, Status Report II', p. 125 ff.
claims.text: Stringfield's consolidated chronology lists as Item B-7 of Status Report II: '1948 or 1950: Mexico, near Del Rio, Texas. Air Force officer observed crashed craft and one body.'
Stringfield acknowledges past funding from the Fund for UFO Research in the acknowledgements to Status Report VII, February 1994.

claims.text: Stringfield acknowledges the cooperation of the J. Allen Hynek Center for UFO Studies in Status Report VII (February 1994) and records consulting its scientific director on 6 November 1993 about the Roswell retrieval body count.

claims.locator: Status Report III, Kingman case notes
claims.sourceText: Stringfield, Status Report III, Kingman case notes
claims.text: Kingman, Arizona 1953 was first investigated and reported by Raymond Fowler; Stringfield referenced it at pages 178-185 of 'Situation Red, The UFO Siege' (Doubleday, 1977) and as Abstract 6 of 'Retrievals of the Third Kind' (1978).

claims.sourceText: Stringfield, Status Report III, Kingman Q&A
claims.text: Stringfield wrote to Fowler on 11 August 1980 seeking permission to question Fowler's source 'Fritz Werner' (pseudonym); Werner's written answers are dated 2 September 1980 and are printed verbatim in Status Report III.

claims.locator: Status Report III, verbatim Q&A dated 2 Sept 1980
claims.sourceText: Stringfield, Status Report III, verbatim Q&A dated 2 September 1980
claims.text: Asked in 1980 for facial detail on the entity, 'Werner' answered: 'Since it's been 27 years, details like this are pretty foggy and I may even be influenced by other descriptions I've seen or heard in the interim.'

DIX-MCGUIRE', concerning an alleged 18 January 1978 incident at McGuire AFB / Fort Dix reported by a USAF Security Police sergeant first published as Case A3 in Status Report III.

claims.locator: Status Report IV, 'Prologue: The Burden of Proof' (scan)
claims.sourceText: Stringfield, Status Report IV, 'Prologue: The Burden of Proof' (scan)
claims.text: Stringfield stated in Status Report IV that public UFO research does not possess proof, and that affidavits, leaked government documents and photographs do not constitute proof - an unusually explicit self-assessment by the field's founding retrieval researcher.
